story: At 9:17 on this humid, hazy Sunday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is inside his garage tightening wiring and testing the light strips on his golf cart at low volume. Donna is texting Gary to confirm Tuesday's two-hour court time and to let him know she has packed him a spare paddle. Hal is sipping his coffee on his porch, content to let the street wake up around him, and Rosa is penciling in a free morning this week for coffee with Hal.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Secure the wiring connections and check the light strips at low volume, all inside the garage
Donna (donna phone): Text Gary to confirm Tuesday's two-hour court time and tell him I packed him a spare paddle
Hal waited: Sipping my coffee on the porch, letting the street wake up and keeping my word about the notebook until Monday.
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Pick a free morning this week and pencil in coffee with Hal

gary.thought_process: Tick 402 I installed the labeled wiring harness and ran a low-volume test. Now it's Sunday morning and nobody's around. The cart is right here in the garage, and I haven't confirmed the test went well or checked the light strips against the L-04 timing. The Architectural Review request is filed, and I'm not going to run anything loud or mount anything visible on the street until they approve (L-01). So the sensible thing is to keep tinkering inside the garage: finish the cart work out of sight, tidy the connections, and make sure everything is ready to go the moment approval comes through. Rosa's dinner is Friday, and I'd love to show Donna the lights then, ideally with approval in hand.

parameters.content: Secure the wiring connections and check the light strips at low volume, all inside the garage

donna.thought_process: I've already penciled in the Tuesday court and packed a spare paddle for Gary, so the logistics are done. Nobody's in sight and it's a hazy Sunday morning. Nothing left to fuss with here, so the next step is to recruit Gary properly. I'll text him through the phone, confirm Tuesday, and remind him about his wrist. L-05 caps me at two hours, which is what I booked.

parameters.content: Text Gary to confirm Tuesday's two-hour court time and tell him I packed him a spare paddle

hal.thought_process: It's Sunday morning, no one is around, and I've been up on the porch already. Dinner at Rosa's settled things for now, and I gave Donna my word the notebook stays in my pocket till Monday. I've scanned the street twice already, so there's no use doing it again. Might as well wait here, finish my coffee, and let the neighborhood wake up on its own. Rules are rules, but a man can rest on a Sunday.

parameters.content: Sipping my coffee on the porch, letting the street wake up and keeping my word about the notebook until Monday.

rosa.thought_process: It's Sunday morning, the dinner is behind me, and nobody is around. I've twice looked over my shift schedule to find a free morning for coffee with Hal, and I promised him in ink this week. I should actually use the schedule object now, pick a morning I'm not on shift, and lock it in so I don't overcommit again.

parameters.content: Pick a free morning this week and pencil in coffee with Hal

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
